newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-NRG Australia on acquisition trail.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-NRG Australia on acquisition trail.

text.p: NRG Australia Ltd, a unit of Northern States Power Co, said on Tuesday it had its eyes firmly on expansion this year, targeting several energy company acquisitions as well as a significant greenfields power project in its Australian home base of Queensland.
"We are pretty hell-bent on acquisitions this year," managing director and chief executive officer, David Scaysbrook told Reuters in an interview.

By the end of 1997, NRG expects to have two power projects established in Indonesia, a "significant" greenfields project in Queensland and involvement in Victoria, New Zealand and Western Australia, Scaysbrook said.
"Our aim is to become a fully-integrated energy company within three years," he said.

NRG is already building an Asian presence with it and the Ansaldo Group of Italy signing a A$650 million joint venture contract late last year to build and operate a 400-megawatt power station in West Java, Indonesia.
Scaysbrook said one or two further projects under the independent power producer (IPP) programme will follow.
However, NRG Australia was currently taking a wait-and-see attitude to initiating greenfields projects in Thailand and the Philippines.
"The structure of the IPP programme means there is pretty fierce competition there," Scaysbrook said.
NRG Australia has established a beachhead in Australia with a 38 percent stake in the Gladstone power station and 50 percent of the Collinsville power station, both in Queensland.
Scaysbrook said the recent merger deal signed by the U.S. parent with Wisconsin Energy Corp meant NRG Australia could now accelerate its growth plans here.
"The merger in the U.S. effectively doubles the (parent) asset base with the new company, Primergy, becoming the tenth largest energy utility in the United States," Scaysbrook said.
"This mean you can double the size of project targets," he said.

Scaysbrook said restructuring of Queensland's electricity supply which has seen AES Transpower Pty Ltd, Transfield Holdings Pty Ltd and Oakey Power Venturers selected as preferred bidders for power supply has meant an active market place.
"What we're going to find in Queensland are those who move fastest with established relationships will be the winners," he said.
"What you are going to see is NRG Australia diversifying," he said.
This meant expansion into gas-fired power supplies and new and innovative power sources, he said.
Increasing IPP criteria also meant companies like NRG Australia would need to have access to energy fuel sources, Scaybrook said.
"We're looking at this," he said.
NRG Australia was not involved in submitting expressions of interest in developing Queensland's Surat Basin coal potential, Scaysbrook said.
"But for the future, fuel is the key," he said.
Meanwhile NRG Australia was very active in co-generation and was developing further projects in this sector, he said.
